title: A small test-only or docs-only scope extension, or a typo fix in a pinned spec, is recorded by firstmate without a new preflight or captain repin card, checked by gate 3 and the reviewer, and listed on the merge card
public_title: Let small test and typo changes skip the repin card
acceptance: Why. Every task runs against a pin: an append-only, hash-checked copy of the approved spec, design and contract, stored under `state/pins/<task>/<version>.json` (`bin/lib/fm_spec_pins.py`). Gate 3, the scope gate, refuses any changed file that no glob in the pinned `scope` list matches (`Pins.scope`, `bin/lib/fm_spec_pins.py` about line 533). Today the only way to add a file to that list is a repin, a new pin version: firstmate amends the spec, runs spec preflight (an isolated review of the spec), raises a captain choice card, waits for the answer, then runs `bin/fm-project.sh repin`, and only then can the next round start. On 2026-10-09 the pull request for the SSH transfer task (T-262, pull request 248) needed its tenth pin and a captain card only to add one file name to one test list. That cost is right for a change of meaning and far too high for a few lines in a test file.

How. This task adds a small-change tier. A small change is either a path record (a few exact files under `tests/`, `docs/` or `README.md` that the pinned scope does not cover) or an erratum (a typo fix in the wording of the pinned title or one acceptance line). firstmate writes a small-change record with one stock command, without spec preflight and without a captain card. Gate 3 accepts a path record within a fixed line budget. The worker and reviewer prompts show every record. The reviewer checks each record against the diff. The merge card lists every record so the captain sees it before the merge click. Every other change, including any production file, any glob, any change of meaning and any external project, keeps the full process: amend, preflight, repin card, repin.

Record store. Records live under `<state>/small-changes/<task>/<n>.json` with `n` counting from 1, beside the pin store and with the same rules: append-only, no symlinks, a `.lock` file taken with `fcntl.flock` while writing, and atomic publication by `os.link` of a fully written temporary file, as `Pins.create` does today (about line 505). A record is never rewritten or deleted by any command.

Record format, common fields. Each record is one JSON object with exactly these keys: `schema` (the integer 1), `project`, `task`, `number` (equal to `n` in the file name), `pin_version` and `pin_sha256` (the SHA-256 of `json.dumps(pin, sort_keys=True)` for the pin it is bound to, the same digest `previous_sha256` uses in the pin chain), `kind` (`paths` or `erratum`), `reason` (an object with non-empty `en` and `zh-TW` strings), `origin` (an object with `kind`, one of `worker-ask`, `review-finding` or `firstmate`, and `ref`, a non-empty single-line string of at most 200 characters that names the source, such as the ask or the review round), `author` (always `firstmate`), `created` (an ISO 8601 UTC time), `previous_sha256` (the SHA-256 of the previous record's file bytes, or null for record 1), and the kind-specific key from the next two requirements.

Record format, path records. A `paths` record adds the key `paths`: a list of 1 to 5 exact repository-relative paths, each at most 200 characters. A path has no glob characters (`*`, `?`, `[`), no `..` part, no leading `/`, no part starting with `.fm-`, and no pinned scope glob already matches it. Each path is `README.md` or starts with `tests/` or `docs/`. No other path is eligible, so `bin/`, `board/`, `skills/`, `design/`, `i18n/`, `config.yaml`, `CONVENTIONS.md`, `.github/` and every task file stay outside the tier.

Record format, errata. An `erratum` record adds the key `erratum`: an object with `field` (`title` or `acceptance`), `index` (the zero-based acceptance index, or null for `title`), `before` (the current wording of that string) and `after` (the corrected wording). The current wording is the pinned string with every earlier erratum of the same pin applied in record order, so two errata on one line chain correctly.

Typo guard. The typo guard is a mechanical eligibility filter. It does not prove that meaning is unchanged; that stays firstmate's judgment when it creates the record and the reviewer's check (see the reviewer requirement). An erratum must keep the meaning of the original, and the record's reason says what the typo was. The filter accepts `after` only when all of these hold. Both strings are split into words and the whitespace between them, and the whitespace sequence is identical, so the word count is equal. At most 3 word positions differ. Each differing pair has a Levenshtein edit distance of at most 2. In each differing pair, after leading `(` and trailing `.,;:!?)` are removed, neither word contains a digit, a backquote, `/`, `_`, `=` or `.`; neither starts with `T-` or `D-`; neither is 7 or more characters made only of the letters a to f (it could be a hexadecimal hash); neither word is the other with letters added only at the start or only at the end (so `valid` to `invalid` and `use` to `user` are refused); and neither is one of these meaning words in any letter case: not, no, never, none, nor, must, may, should, shall, can, cannot, only, all, any, every, each, without, unless. This guard is deliberately stricter than the rewrite guard the plain-writing task (T-270, pull request 260) adds for spec preflight, and this task neither imports nor changes that guard. `public_title`, `scope`, `depends_on` and every other spec key cannot take an erratum.

Limit per pin. A pin version has at most 3 small-change records of either kind. A fourth needs the full process. firstmate folds the earlier records into the amended spec at that repin: the record paths join `scope` and the errata are applied to the text.

Who creates a record. Only firstmate, through one new stock command run outside any round: `bin/fm-project.sh small-change --project

--task --origin --ref --reason-en --reason-tw (--path ... | --erratum --after ) [--repo ]`. It resolves the current pin through `Pins.resolve`, binds the record to that pin, checks every record rule above (format, path eligibility, typo guard, the limit per pin and the reason text), and prints the record JSON. It does not look at any diff: the line budget and binary check belong to gate 3, which has the head and base. It exits 64 for a malformed argument (an unknown option, a missing required option, both `--path` and `--erratum`, neither of them, or an unknown `--origin` kind) and 65 with a one-line reason for any refusal. It also refuses with 65 while the task holds merge authority: a pending merge card for this task and project (a `state/pending/` record of kind `merge` or `merge-untracked`, refused with `a merge card is pending; let the captain answer it first`), or an answered merge card for this task with choice A whose outcome is not `failed` (running or merged, read with the same `merge_outcome` rule `merge_blocker` uses in `bin/lib/fm_concurrent.py` about line 263, refused with `the captain already approved a merge for this task`). After a merge failed, or after the captain answered B (hold) or C (ask for a fix), a record may be created, but the existing hold rules in `failed_card_evidence()` (`bin/lib/fm_autopilot_loop.py` about line 112) do not change and a record never lifts them. After B or C, both the same head and any new head stay held exactly as today. After a failed A merge, only the existing verified failed-card replacement on a different head (T-269) can raise a new merge card, and that card discloses the record. So a record never changes what a waiting or approved card should have shown. The pending check and the record publication run while the command holds `state/merge-turn.lock`, the same lock that `MechanicalLoop.merge_card` holds from preparing the details to requesting the card (`bin/lib/fm_autopilot_loop.py` about line 631, `bin/lib/fm_concurrent.py` about line 270). The lock order is always `merge-turn.lock` first, then the record store's `.lock`; the merge loop never takes the record store's `.lock`. So a record is either published before the merge loop reads the records (and is disclosed) or refused because the card is pending or approved. It refuses inside a round (`FM_IN_ROUND` set, as `bin/fm-canary.sh` about line 101 does), so a worker or reviewer cannot create a record; the round sandbox also hides the engine's `state/` directory from the round (`bin/lib/fm_sandbox_policy.py`, `pinned_state`, about line 188). The autopilot never creates a record.

Reason text and representability. `--reason-en` is at most 200 characters and `--reason-tw` at most 120 characters. Before writing a record, the command renders the exact `en` and `zh-TW` note that the merge card will show for it (the disclosure requirement defines the text, with the review status shown as `not checked by the review`, the longer variant), and checks each note with the same sentence and length checks that `check_details` in `bin/lib/fm_ste.py` (the STE writing rules for card text) applies to a `notes` item. It refuses the record when either fails. So every admitted record can be shown on a merge card by itself.

Self project only. With `FM_EXTERNAL=1` the command exits 64 with `small-change tier is self-project only; use the full process`. Every reader (gate 3 in `Pins.scope`, the prompt renderer, the autopilot fingerprint and the merge card disclosure) checks `FM_EXTERNAL` (or the autopilot's external project context) first and, for an external project, never opens, lists or validates the record store, whether it is valid, corrupt or a symlink. External projects keep their private-state rules unchanged, and no record or reason text can reach an external repository, pull request, comment or event.

No event and no card. Creating a record emits no event and raises no card, so `bin/fm-emit.sh`, `bin/fm-diagram.sh` and `bin/fm-decide.sh` are unchanged. The merge card is the captain's view of every record (see the merge card requirement).

Gate 3 accepts path records. `Pins.scope` first runs every check it runs today. For each changed path that no pinned glob matches, it accepts the path only when a valid `paths` record bound to the resolved pin (same `pin_version` and `pin_sha256`) lists it exactly; otherwise it refuses with today's `out of scope: <path>` message. Paths starting with `.fm-` stay refused whatever a record says.

Gate 3 line budget. After the path check, gate 3 runs `git diff --no-renames --numstat <base>...<head> -- <every path accepted through a record>`. It refuses when the total added lines exceed 20, when the total removed lines exceed 20 (removing test lines can weaken a suite as much as adding them), or when any of those paths is binary (`-` in the numstat counts). The refusal names the totals, for example `small-change budget exceeded: +23 -0 (limit +20 -20)`. The limits are constants in `bin/lib/fm_small_change.py`, not configuration.

Gate 3 validates the store. When the store directory for the task exists, gate 3 validates every record in it before it uses any. Structure: the directory, every record file and the `.lock` file are not symlinks; each file name is `<n>.json` and equals `number`; numbering starts at 1 with no gap; the `previous_sha256` chain holds; the key set is exactly the one defined above with no extra or missing key; `schema`, `number` and `pin_version` are JSON integers (not booleans or strings); an erratum's `index` is exactly null when `field` is `title`, and a non-boolean JSON integer from 0 to the last acceptance index of the bound pin's spec when `field` is `acceptance`; `project` and `task` equal the gate's project and task; `created` parses as an ISO 8601 UTC time; and `origin`, `reason` and `author` have the shapes defined above. History: each record is checked against the pin version it names, not against the latest pin. The named version must exist in the task's verified pin chain (a version above the latest is refused), and `pin_sha256` must equal that version's digest. Path eligibility (including 'no pinned glob already matches it') and the erratum `before` text are checked against that pin's spec, with the earlier errata bound to the same version applied. The limit of 3 counts per pin version. To get every verified version, `bin/lib/fm_spec_pins.py` gains a method that returns the whole chain that `Pins.resolve` already walks; `resolve` itself keeps its return value. A record that fails any check makes gate 3 refuse with `invalid small-change record <n>: <reason>`; it is never skipped silently. Only after the whole store validates does gate 3 keep the records bound to the latest pin and ignore the rest, so after a repin the task returns to its new pinned scope.

Lazy import. `bin/lib/fm_spec_pins.py` and `bin/lib/fm_prompt_context.py` import `fm_small_change` only inside the code path that runs when `<state>/small-changes/<task>` exists. Test fixtures that copy `fm_spec_pins.py` without the new module, such as `tests/lib/autopilot_entrypoints.py` (about line 32) and `tests/lib/project-storage.sh` (line 11), therefore keep working unchanged.

Worker and reviewer see the records. `bin/lib/fm_prompt_context.py` `render()`, which writes the pinned part of every worker and reviewer prompt, adds a section `# Small changes recorded for this pin` after the design section anchors whenever valid records exist for the current pin. For each path record it lists the record number, the first 12 hex digits of the record file's SHA-256, the paths, the reason and the budget (`+20 -20` lines in total across all record paths), and says these paths may be changed in addition to the scope list. For each erratum it shows the field, the corrected wording and the sentence `The corrected wording is the meaning; the pinned bytes are unchanged.` With no records the output is byte-for-byte what it is today, so `tests/lib/review_pinned_golden.py` and `tests/pinned-context.test.sh` pass unchanged.

Reviewer checks each record. `skills/reviewer/SKILL.md`, check 3 ('Does anything reach outside the declared scope?'), adds: for each small-change record in the prompt, check that the diff in its paths matches its reason, touches only test or documentation content, and does not change what any acceptance line requires; for an erratum, check that the corrected wording means the same as the original. When a record passes, the verdict contains one line that is exactly `SMALL-CHANGE-CHECKED:<task> <n> <sha12>` (the record number and the first 12 hex digits of the record file's SHA-256, as the prompt shows them), standing alone and not quoted, placed above the numbered standing list when there is one, never inside it. When a record fails, the reviewer reports a finding instead. `criteria()` and `protocol()` in `bin/lib/fm_evidence.py` are unchanged, and a regression test shows that a verdict carrying these lines parses exactly as before.

Merge card disclosure. In `MechanicalLoop.merge_card` (`bin/lib/fm_autopilot_loop.py` about line 622), after the details file is chosen (firstmate's authored details or the built ones), the autopilot reads the valid records for the task's current pin, for the self project only. When there are any, it writes a copy of the chosen details to `state/decision-details-built/<id>.json` with, in both `en` and `zh-TW`, one `notes` item of kind `caution` per record and one question asking whether the captain accepts the listed small changes, then requests the card with that copy. The note text is fixed by `bin/lib/fm_small_change.py`: the record number, its kind, its paths or erratum field, its reason, and `checked by the review` or `not checked by the review`. firstmate's authored file is never modified. With no records the request is byte-for-byte what it is today.

Review status on the card. A record counts as checked only when the approving verdict for the gated head (the latest verdict from `MechanicalLoop.verdict`, about line 245, with verdict `APPROVE` and `head` equal to the gated head) contains, as a standalone line outside quoted text (the existing `unquoted()` reader in `bin/lib/fm_evidence.py`, about line 26), exactly `SMALL-CHANGE-CHECKED:<task> <n> <sha12>` for this task, this record number and this record's hash. A line for another task, another number or another hash, a line inside a quote, and a line in a verdict for an older head do not count. An unchecked record, for example one created after the approving review or one the reviewer did not mark, does not block: it shows on the merge card as `not checked by the review`. The card still goes up; the captain decides on the board. Merge authority is unchanged: every merge still needs the captain's click.

Disclosure that does not fit. The autopilot runs `check_details(kind='merge')` of `bin/lib/fm_ste.py` on the combined copy before requesting the card. If the combined details fail any check, including the item counts (at most 12 notes and 6 questions), the autopilot drops nothing and requests nothing: it raises the existing `details` attention, `<task> ready: merge card details needed (<id>): small-change disclosure does not fit: <first checker failure>`. Because each record's note passed the same checks when the record was created and a pin has at most 3 records, firstmate can always fix this by authoring details with fewer notes or questions of its own.

A new record wakes the merge path. In `advance()` (`bin/lib/fm_autopilot_loop.py` about line 448), the list `inputs` that is hashed into the advancement fingerprint gains, for the self project and only when `<state>/small-changes/<task>` exists, one more element appended last (after the failed-card replacement element when there is one): the SHA-256 of the record files' bytes in number order. So a record created after gate 3 failed on a head makes the autopilot run the gates again on that same head. With no store the inputs list, and so every existing fingerprint, is unchanged. The new element only lets the gates run again; every hold that `advance()` checks before the fingerprint, including same-head failure and answered B or C cards, still applies first. A record cannot be created while a merge card is pending or approved (see the command requirement).

firstmate's rules. `skills/firstmate/SKILL.md` gains a short subsection 'Small changes' next to 'Spec preflight before dispatch and repin': when a SCOPE-BLOCKED or ASK request from a worker (a standalone marker line in `.fm-say.md` that wakes firstmate), a review finding, or firstmate's own reading needs only test or documentation lines in exact paths within the budget, or only a typo fix, firstmate creates the record with the command, briefs the next round with the record number, and raises no card. Anything else stays a board scope card, as today. Standing order 4 and the sentence near line 26 that scope decisions remain board decisions name this tier as the one exception. The subsection also says to fold records into the spec at the next repin.

Worker rules. `skills/worker/SKILL.md` changes in three places. In the gate 3 paragraph (about line 38), the diff may also touch the exact paths of small-change records listed in the prompt, within their budget; any other file outside the globs still means writing `.fm-say.md` and stopping. In the role-boundary paragraph (about line 247), scope changes remain board decisions except the small-change records firstmate creates; a worker never creates a record or widens scope itself. Where it describes the `SCOPE-BLOCKED:<task>` marker (about line 219), it adds: when the request is for test or documentation files, name each exact path and the expected added and removed line counts, so firstmate can judge the tier at once.

Design. `design/design.md` gets four edits, each inside its numbered section. Section 6 (Lifecycle and the gates) gets a new subsection `### Small changes (T-277)` at the end of the section, after the subsection 'Spec preflight and migration (T-185)' and before `## 7`, describing the record store, format, typo guard, limits, creator, gate 3 rule, prompts, reviewer line and merge card disclosure. Section 15.5 (Immutable pins and authoritative heads) amends the sentence 'Gate 3 refuses missing pins, mismatches, out-of-scope files and `.fm-*` artifacts' (about line 5704) to name the small-change exception. Section 15.8 (Pilot and advanced integration), in the paragraph on advancement fingerprints (about line 6251, 'An unchanged fingerprint holds across restarts'), adds that a self task with a small-change store appends one record-store digest after any failed-card replacement evidence, that without a store the input stays byte-equivalent, and that same-head failure and answered cards still hold. Section 8 (The captain's board), in the paragraph on card kinds that describes the merge card (about line 2375), adds that a merge card lists every small-change record.

Migration. No pin, preflight receipt, verdict, decision or card is rewritten, and no stored format changes; the record store is new and starts empty. Tasks in flight, including T-262, can use the tier as soon as this change merges, bound to their current pin. Gates and launchers running older frozen code ignore the store, so for them a path outside scope still fails gate 3: the change fails closed, never open. A repin needs no change: records bound to the older pin are ignored afterwards. Reverting this change leaves records on disk, unread, and every such task falls back to its pinned scope.

Tests, new behaviour. A new suite, `tests/small-change.test.sh` with `tests/lib/small_change_cases.py`, declares its dependencies in its header comment like the other suites. These named cases drive entry points that exist on the current base, so on the base they fail at a behavioural assertion, not at an import error or unknown flag: gate 3 through `python3 bin/lib/fm_spec_pins.py scope` accepts a test file listed in a planted valid record (base refuses with `out of scope`); `python3 bin/lib/fm_prompt_context.py pin worker` and `pin reviewer` print the small-changes section for a planted record and an erratum (base prints none); and the autopilot merge path, through the fixtures of `tests/lib/autopilot_merge_path.py`, requests a merge card whose `notes` and questions disclose the record in both locales, with `checked by the review` when the approving verdict carries the line and `not checked by the review` when it does not (base discloses nothing).

Tests, gate 3 refusals and record integrity. Named cases in `tests/lib/small_change_cases.py` show gate 3 refuses: a record path under `bin/` planted by hand; a glob path; a path already matched by the bound pin's scope; 6 paths in one record; a path over 200 characters; a `.fm-` path; a fourth record for one pin; a numbering gap; a file name that disagrees with `number`; an extra key; a missing key; a wrong project; a wrong task; `number` or `pin_version` given as a string or a boolean; a title erratum with an integer `index`; an acceptance erratum with a null, boolean, negative or out-of-range `index`; a malformed `created`; an unknown `origin.kind`; an empty `origin.ref`; a broken `previous_sha256` chain; a symlinked record file, record directory or `.lock` file; a `pin_version` above the latest pin; a `pin_sha256` that matches no version or the wrong version; and an erratum whose `before` is stale. Budget cases: exactly +20 and exactly -20 in total across two record paths pass; +21 or -21 in total, split across two paths, is refused; a binary file is refused. History and errata cases show: two errata on one acceptance line chain in record order and the prompt shows the final wording; a record bound to an older pin version is ignored after its validation, so the same path is refused again after a repin; after a repin that folds both a path record and an erratum into the new spec, the retained old records still validate against their own pin version (the path was not in that older scope, the `before` matches that older text), even though the path is now in scope; and the limit of 3 starts again for the new pin version.

Tests, the command and the typo guard. These are interface tests, labelled so, because on the base the subcommand and module do not exist; they are not counted as fail-first evidence. `bin/fm-project.sh small-change` writes a valid record of each kind and prints it. It exits 64 for an unknown option, a missing `--task`, `--reason-en` or `--origin`, both `--path` and `--erratum`, neither of them, an unknown `--origin` kind, and `FM_EXTERNAL=1`. It exits 65 with `FM_IN_ROUND=1`, for each record rule above that does not need a diff, for a reason over the length limit, for a reason whose rendered note fails the STE check in either locale, and while a merge card for the task is pending. A title erratum with a null `index` is accepted. The typo guard accepts `recieve` to `receive` and `teh` to `the`, and refuses a changed number, a changed path, a changed code span, a changed task ID, `deadbeef` to `deadbeee`, `valid` to `invalid`, `must` to `may`, adding or removing `not`, a changed word count, changed whitespace and four changed words.

Tests, merge card. Through the fixtures of `tests/lib/autopilot_merge_path.py`, named cases show: the authored details file in `state/decision-details/` is byte-for-byte unchanged after a disclosed request; the request uses the copy in `state/decision-details-built/`; a record counts as checked only for the exact standalone line, and a line with the wrong task, wrong number or wrong hash, a quoted line, or a line in a verdict for an older head leaves it `not checked by the review`; details with 12 notes of their own, or 6 questions of their own, raise the `details` attention and request nothing; both locales carry the same number of notes and questions; a controlled interleaving, with the merge loop holding `state/merge-turn.lock` while the command waits, shows the record is either disclosed on the card or refused as pending, never published unseen; the command refuses after the captain answered A while the merge runs and after it merged; after an answer of B or C the command writes the record, and both the same head and a new head stay held across a poll and an autopilot restart with no new card; after a failed A merge the command writes the record, the same head stays held, and a new head with verified failed-card replacement history gets a card that discloses the record; and the existing held-card cases in `tests/lib/autopilot_loop.py` (about line 940) pass unchanged. In `advance()`, a record created after a gate 3 failure on an unchanged head changes the fingerprint and starts a new gate run, and a task with no store keeps exactly the fingerprint it has on the base.

Tests, external isolation. With `FM_EXTERNAL=1` and a planted store that is valid, corrupt or a symlink, each holding a private sentinel string: gate 3 refuses the path as out of scope exactly as today and never mentions the store; the worker and reviewer prompts do not contain the sentinel; the autopilot's external merge path does not read the store and no card request, event or attention text contains the sentinel; and the store's files keep their bytes and modification times.

Tests, migration. Named cases show: a task with an existing pin, a SPEC-OK preflight receipt, a verdict and an answered dispatch card gains a record, and gate 3 then accepts the path with no new preflight or repin, while the bytes of the pin, receipt, verdict and decision files are unchanged; the base version of `bin/lib/fm_spec_pins.py` (read with `git show` from the base commit into a temporary copy) run against a non-empty store still refuses the path as out of scope, which is both the frozen old-code case and the rollback case; and after that rollback run the store files are unchanged.

Tests, regressions. Behaviour the base already has is labelled regression: gate 3 without any record store refuses out-of-scope and `.fm-` paths exactly as today; the reviewer prompt golden in `tests/lib/review_pinned_golden.py` is unchanged; `criteria()` and `protocol()` read a verdict with `SMALL-CHANGE-CHECKED` lines exactly as before; a merge request for a task without records is byte-for-byte unchanged; and the copy fixtures named in the lazy-import requirement pass. These existing suites pass unchanged and are not edited: `tests/spec-pins.test.sh`, `tests/pinned-context.test.sh`, `tests/autopilot-merge-path.test.sh`, `tests/gate.test.sh`, `tests/autopilot-entrypoints.test.sh`, `tests/decide.test.sh` (its check near line 1098 that only `bin/fm.sh` and the autopilot merge loop raise cards still holds, because the new command raises none).

Coordination. These in-flight tasks touch the same files and none is a dependency; whichever merges second rebases and keeps both. The plain-writing task (T-270, pull request 260) changes `bin/lib/fm_autopilot_loop.py` merge card text, `skills/firstmate/SKILL.md`, `skills/reviewer/SKILL.md`, `skills/worker/SKILL.md` and `design/design.md`; its spec rewrite guard is separate from this task's typo guard. The reviewer-fixes task (T-272, pull request 261) changes `bin/lib/fm_autopilot_loop.py`, both skills and `design/design.md`; a concrete fix it attaches that needs a test path outside scope is a natural `review-finding` origin for this tier. The live-view task (T-271, pull request 259) and the retrospective task (T-273) touch `skills/firstmate/SKILL.md`, `skills/reviewer/SKILL.md` and `design/design.md` only in other sections. The flaky-test task (T-274) has no spec yet.

Out of scope. No change to the six gates other than gate 3's record check, to spec preflight, to repin, to the pin format, to `bin/fm-worker.sh`, `bin/fm-review.sh`, `bin/fm-decide.sh` or the board, and no small-change tier for external projects. The pinned spec bytes and the task file never change through an erratum; the fix reaches the task file at the next ordinary repin.
